issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)), but the provided solution and example Main use and provide a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and may cause tests or examples to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent: either (A) update the solution and example Main to implement and use SealSaloon(String name) (i.e., add a String parameter to the constructor and initialize fields accordingly), or (B) change the problem statement/UML to specify a no-argument constructor. Ensure all examples and tests use the same constructor signature.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify a SealSaloon constructor taking a String (SealSaloon(String)), but the example Main and the reference solution use a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch in the constructor signature for the same conceptual entity (the SealSaloon class) creates ambiguity for students about the required class API and where to provide the saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the constructor signature across all artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and Main to implement and call SealSaloon(String) (and store the name field), matching the UML and problem text, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to show a no-argument constructor so it matches the provided Main and solution. Ensure all examples and tests use the same constructor signature.
